Cache

Use Cache-Control no-store on Clincoo Account Pages

Cached account HTML can show someone else's data after Back. no-store stops copies in the CDN and browser.

This article is available in: Indonesia · English

Profile, cart, and form-result pages often inherit static-asset cache headers. A visitor hits Back and sees an email or token that is not theirs.

Set Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate on documents that hold session data. Keep CSS, fonts, and images immutable.

In editor.clincoo.buzz preview, test with Disable cache off, then use Back. Account content must be requested again from origin, not read from disk.

Do not rely on a Pragma meta tag in HTML. CDNs honor response headers from your host or a Cloudflare _headers file.

Ask the AI to add header rules only for /akun or /app paths. Do not change font max-age that is already correct.
